operation_type.description: Provide the operation type. Allowed values: Create, Modify. Synonyms must be normalized to the canonical value.
operation_type.x-a2at-value-constraint: Allowed canonical values: Create, Modify. Normalize synonyms to the canonical value instead of treating them as out-of-range: Add / Implement / Establish / Deploy / Set Up / Provision / New / Enable / Activate / Configure are all Create; Update / Adjust / Change / Revise / Edit are all Modify.

task_description.description: Dynamically provide the task description based on the operation type (Create/Modify).
examples: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), output a wireless network energy saving plan that achieves the wireless network energy saving goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target), and return the wireless network energy saving result in the format defined in [Expected Output](#expected-output).
task_description.x-a2at-value-constraint: When the type is [Create]: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), output a wireless network energy saving plan that achieves the wireless network energy saving goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target), and return the wireless network energy saving result in the format defined in [Expected Output](#expected-output). When the type is [Modify]: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), output a wireless network energy saving plan that achieves the wireless network energy saving goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target). The value must always be non-null. Output the fixed text verbatim; there is no need to replace [Task Object](#task-object), [Task Context](#task-context), [Task Target](#task-target) or [Expected Output](#expected-output) with actual slot values — these are in-document anchor links, not placeholders.

task_object.description: Explicitly specify the energy saving coverage scope information, a geographic or logical area (e.g., district-level administrative unit). The area information is a required parameter.
examples: The area is the Songshanhu Administration Committee.
task_object.x-a2at-value-constraint: Area name. A named region (a specific region name such as "A2ATestRegion" or "Slice A") is valid. Only anonymous vague descriptions that carry no concrete region name, such as "test area", "sites in this area", "all communities", "indoor communities", or "outdoor communities", must report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Area' and actual describing what is missing. Only one region name is allowed; if the input specifies multiple regions, report slot.constraint_violated.

task_target.description: Define the quantitative or qualitative goals the task must achieve. Quantitative and qualitative goals cannot be selected at the same time, and the default is a qualitative goal.
task_target.x-a2at-value-constraint: 1. Quantitative goal: energy saving gain target as a single percentage (e.g. 30%). A range is NOT a single value — you MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Energy saving gain target'. Range formats include '20%-30%', '20% - 30%', '20% ~ 30%', '20% to 30%'. 2. Qualitative goal: maximize energy saving under the task context conditions. The mode must be one of Aggressive, Conservative, Lossless Experience, Lossy Experience (synonyms are listed in the [terminology] section below); other values (e.g. 'green', 'eco', 'balanced', 'auto') report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Energy saving mode'. A numeric throughput/rate/UX target is a rate guarantee goal, not a mode, and must not be treated as a mode violation. A phrase like 'maximize the rate' or 'maximize the rate as much as possible' is a vague rate guarantee goal, NOT an energy saving mode — do NOT report it as a mode violation.

task_context.description: Provide the background and context information for task execution.
examples: Cell RAT for energy saving: NR; Energy saving time range: start time "08:00:00", end time "12:00:00"; Time-segmented rate guarantee goal: {00:00~06:00,2Mbps}, {06:00~18:00,10Mbps}.
task_context.x-a2at-value-constraint:
Apply these rules in order. Each rule gives the trigger condition and the error to report. You MUST report the error when the trigger is met; do NOT silently fix, normalize, or extract the value as valid.
1. Cell RAT: only LTE, NR, LNR, all are valid (synonyms in [terminology] below). Invalid values such as '3G', '2G', 'WiFi' MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Cell RAT'. Do NOT rewrite an invalid RAT to a valid one (e.g. do NOT change '3G' to 'NR').
2. Cross-task reference: if the input mentions TWO or more earlier/previous tasks and uses a phrase like 'same as the previous task' WITHOUT specifying which one to inherit from, the reference is ambiguous. You MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Task reference'. Do NOT silently pick one candidate; set value to null.
3. Energy saving time range, recurring daily; if omitted, full-period energy saving. Rate goal is guaranteed only within this range.
4. Carrier frequencies that can be turned off. When the input mentions turning off / shutting down carrier frequencies (e.g. 'turn off the carrier frequencies', 'shut down carrier') but does NOT provide specific frequency numbers (e.g. 1600, 1650), you MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Carrier frequencies'. A frequency must be an exact number (e.g. 1600). Words like 'approximately', 'about', 'around', 'centered at approximately' before a frequency make it an approximation — you MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Carrier frequencies'. Do NOT remove the approximation word and extract the number as if it were exact.
5. Rate guarantee goal: minimum downlink throughput target and its effective time period. Area-level supports time-segmented/full-period; site-level requires site list, time-segmented rate goal, and optional background event and duration. Time windows MUST NOT overlap and must fall within the energy-saving execution period; overlapping windows report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Time windows'. Time period names such as 'idle period', 'regular period', 'busy period', 'peak period', 'off-peak period' are NOT explicit clock ranges — you MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Time windows'. A vague rate (e.g. 'maximize the rate' without a number) reports slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Guaranteed rate'. When the input says rate targets 'need to be adjusted' / 'need to change' / 'need to be modified' / uses an imperative like 'modify the guaranteed throughput target' and specifies a time range (e.g. 'adjusted from 08:00 to 12:00') but does NOT give a specific rate value (e.g. 10Mbps), you MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Guaranteed rate'. The presence of a time range without a rate value is the trigger. The time range may be stated explicitly (e.g. 'from 08:00 to 12:00') OR referenced indirectly (e.g. 'during the outage', 'during the energy saving period' — these refer back to a previously stated time range and count as a time range). A general 'modify the throughput target' request with neither an explicit nor an indirect time range nor a rate value is acceptable.
6. In outage/modify scenarios (when the input mentions 'power outage'), the affected site list and outage time are REQUIRED. (a) Site list: must be concrete site names. If the input mentions a power outage but does NOT list specific site names (e.g. 'Modify the energy-saving plan in A2ATestRegion region. A power outage will occur...'), you MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Site list'. An area name alone is NOT a site list. A count of sites without names (e.g. '10 sites', '5 base stations') means the site list is unspecified — report slot.not_provided (NOT slot.constraint_violated) with slot_label 'Site list'. The value is missing, not invalid. References to sites by area or scope without concrete names (e.g. 'sites in this area', 'all affected sites', 'sites in the region') are NOT a concrete site list — report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Site list'. Site names introduced as examples without a complete list ('sites such as X and Y', 'sites like X', 'e.g. X') MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Site list', even if other errors (e.g. Area violation) are also present. A phrase like 'and a few others' appended to concrete site names indicates the site list is incomplete — the user has not enumerated all affected sites. You MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Site list'. (b) Outage time: must be a concrete clock range (e.g. 'from 08:00 to 12:00'). If the input only gives a relative date (e.g. 'tomorrow') without a clock range, report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Outage start/end time'. If a clock range is given with a relative date (e.g. 'from 08:00 to 12:00 tomorrow'), that is acceptable — only the clock range is required, not the date. Outage duration must be a single specific number (e.g. 3 hours), not a range (e.g. '2 or 3 hours'); ranges report slot.constraint_violated.

expected_output.description: When the task object is a geographic/logical area, output the intent report for the network energy saving task.
expected_output.x-a2at-value-constraint: Basic information about the intent execution result: area, intent goal achievement status. Detailed information about the intent execution result: energy saving gain achievement status (current energy saving gain goal, actual energy saving gain percentage, target adjustment suggestions), rate goal achievement status (current rate goal, actual rate, target adjustment suggestions).
